clue.text: One has Bond smashing luge into pieces

indicators.note: something broken into pieces can be put back together in a different order

blocks.note: smashing and super are both British slang for excellent
the sledge, taken as letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: James Bond wrecks a racing sledge in an action sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' with its capital looks like 007, but it is the ordinary noun for adhesion; 'smashing' sounds like the destruction but simply means excellent.

clue.text: Close result — disastrous conclusion

blocks.note: close weather is humid and muggy, which is sticky
an end is an outcome or result

explanation.surface: A tight contest finishes in calamity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close result' reads as a narrow win, but close here is the weather sense, muggy.

clue.text: Online contributor on beer absorbing a creative product

blocks.note: someone who posts messages on an internet forum
a pint is a glass of beer in British pubs
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: In British pubs beer comes by the pint, so the glass size stands for the drink; 'creative product' is a deliberately vague definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Poster paint is a cheap opaque colour used by children and artists, so it is a product for creative work.

clue.text: Academician and Knight Companion arriving at farm

blocks.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
N is the chess notation for a knight
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Two distinguished honours holders turn up at a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knight Companion' looks like a single title, but it splits into two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm, especially one raising cattle in North America.

clue.text: Opening yard by church good for carrying in deceased

indicators.note: carrying something in means holding it inside, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: the late someone is a person who has died
Y is the abbreviation for yard
CH is the abbreviation for church
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A churchyard entrance is used for bringing in the dead for burial.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue fits the scene: a lychgate is where the coffin once rested before a funeral, and lych is an old word for corpse.

clue.text: Thrill having caught the thing in Devon river

C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
it is the pronoun for a thing

explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' sounds like fishing, but it is the cricket abbreviation; C and IT go inside EXE.

clue.text: Appeal forces landowner to regenerate location in Essex

taken as letters to be rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: Doubling a letter abbreviation to make a plural, as with FF for forces, is a standard convention. Essex is a county north-east of London.

clue.text: Stigma — a mark that hurt blustery old coward

blocks.note: a scar is a lasting mark of disgrace, a stigma
taken as written

the cry someone makes when something hurts

explanation.walkthrough: 'that hurt' reads as describing the mark, but it stands for the exclamation itself.

clue.text: One supervising Sellers in Goon realm, far gone

explanation.definitionFit: A floor manager in a store oversees the sales assistants working on the shop floor.

clue.text: East German comes in ready to make swift reply

clue.text: Celestial phenomenon stars follow and not sailors?

stars are lights in the night sky

explanation.walkthrough: RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's naval force; with THE in front it stands for the sailors as a body.

clue.text: Firm accessing a large population provides drink

the first three letters, the informal clipped form used in phrases like pop. 8,000

clue.text: Man facing surgery has nothing to lose in hopeless state

clue.text: Accessible content of online article

clue.text: Dramatist in one book Sterne regularly shunned

a hoop is a circular band, as on a barrel

blocks.note: a rick is a stack of hay, a heap

taken as written

clue.text: Photograph enrages sheik when developed — it’s really small

clue.text: See tailless canine hero, one revered as god

blocks.note: taken as written, before its last letter goes

clue.text: Feats from retired airmen one moved along

taken as letters to be rearranged

clue.text: Wild thing preferring squash to snakebite?

clue.text: I’m obliged to exercise caution, handling large knives etc

indicators.note: handling something means holding it, so one piece grips another

blocks.note: ta is British slang for thank you
to beware is to be careful
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone grateful must take care when handling big blades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'large knives' reads as one phrase, but large is just a letter and knives belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tableware is the dishes, cutlery and glasses used at a meal, so knives are one example.

blocks.note: the opening letter
Mass is a church service

explanation.walkthrough: 'service' sounds like a restaurant or shop, but it is a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather or accumulate a large amount over time.

clue.text: Valuable box certain to be found among the crates at sea

indicators.note: being at sea is being confused and adrift, so the letters are mixed up
being among things means sitting in the middle of them, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: taken as letters to be rearranged
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A precious box is bound to turn up among the cargo crates on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' fits the ship's cargo so well that it hides as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasure chest is a strongbox holding gold and jewels, so it is a box of great worth.

clue.text: Philosopher and some things to mark his birthday?

definitions.text: some things to mark his birthday?

blocks.note: first meaning: the French thinker of 'I think, therefore I am'

blocks.clueFragment: some things to mark his birthday?
blocks.note: second meaning: put the phrase 'some cards' into French, the philosopher's own language

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a pun: split and read in French, the name becomes 'some cards', fitting since he was French.
explanation.definitionFit: René Descartes was the French rationalist philosopher; birthday greetings are sent as cards, cartes in French.
